A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, figures, equations, and Appendices A–E. The corresponding claims, constructions, and proofs can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results and proofs, including in its appendices. Its reproducibility statement explicitly describes all results as theoretical; the arithmetic illustration is not an experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical results without adding original empirical outcomes. Section 4's new empirical-validation paragraph cites other researchers' findings and proposes targeted experiments as future work.

M1.justification: The planner–predictor formulation, resampling mechanism, parallel CoT, stochastic padded looped transformers, and simulation constructions remain unchanged. The expanded discussion does not introduce a new component or procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version reports datasets or tasks actually used for empirical training or evaluation. Formal-language recognition and other problem classes remain theoretical subjects; v2's proposed benchmarks are future work.

E2.justification: CoT, parallel CoT, and padded looped transformers remain the same theoretical comparison frameworks. Neither version evaluates an empirical baseline suite, and the new citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version contains experimental splits, evaluation metrics, training budgets, or testing procedures. The formal precision, width, and computational-resource assumptions are retained.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or error analyses are added or removed. The new discussion of modular-counting sensitivity cites prior work rather than presenting an additional analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained stochastic sampling definitions do not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: No measured results are added or revised, and the stated theoretical bounds remain unchanged. The arithmetic illustration retains three parallel versus eleven sequential steps, moving from v1 Figure 2 to v2 Figure 3.

T1.justification: v2 adds a missing minus sign to the upper bound in subcase 2c of Lemma D.7's proof, correcting the negative-score case (v1 page 28; v2 page 29). This is a localized mathematical correction; the theorem statements and constructions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory takeaways, and conclusion retain the same contributions: MDM–PLT equivalence, mutual simulation with CoT, complexity-class characterizations, and the sequentiality bottleneck separating efficient MDM and CoT reasoning.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly distinguishes expressivity from learnability, discusses the difficulty of learning the ideal planner, and qualifies the available empirical implications. Its expanded positional-encoding discussion largely develops explanations already present in v1 Appendix D.1.

D1.justification: The formal construction details and reproducibility statement directing readers to Appendices D–E are retained. The expanded positional-encoding explanation does not disclose a new implementation setting, and no code, data-access, or resource information is added.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hahn and Rofin (2024) to support the learnability discussion and Ye et al. (2025) as empirical motivation. The existing related-work comparisons and central novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, expands Section 4 with dedicated discussion paragraphs, adds an acknowledgment, and replaces the preprint header with the ICLR publication header. The main section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v1's combined Figure 1 is reorganized into v2 Figures 1–2, separating model relationships from complexity-class relationships and adding colored source/target constraint labels with explanatory captions. The arithmetic illustration is retained as Figure 3, with accompanying page reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the theory easier to assess through explicit learnability and empirical-applicability qualifications in Section 4, clearer constraint labels in Figures 1–2, and the corrected proof condition in Lemma D.7. These provide limited improvements in transparency, presentation, and mathematical accuracy while preserving the central results.
